reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes paid OneCoin packages that generate tokens, links purchases and participant enrollment to commissions, multi-level bonuses, network advancement, and rank prizes, and urges earlier entry for greater value. A rapid income-replacement testimonial reinforces this promotional appeal, while the future-value estimate is expressly uncertain.

citations.quote: pack at 130 Euro. Trader, 530. ProTrader, 1030. Executive, 3030. And Tycoon at 5,030.
each package that you purchase gets so many mining tokens that convert into OneCoin
it pays you a percentage of your team of those personally connected to you, four levels deep, four levels away from you
I would be paid an override on each one of their network bonuses as their leg bonus

opening.argument: Judge, the future-value discussion is presented as a conditional estimate, not a promised return. The speaker calls the scenarios optimistic and base cases, then explicitly says nobody knows what will happen. That qualification matters: the figures are offered as a forecast to evaluate, not a guaranteed payout. A speculative presentation can be overly enthusiastic without establishing that its forecast is being passed off as certain.

citations.quote: this is an optimistic and a base scenario
We don't have any idea what's going to happen in the future. Nobody does.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited package prices and token conversion establish what the speaker says a buyer receives; they do not turn the expressly uncertain future-value estimate into a guarantee. Likewise, a description of team percentages establishes compensation terms, not that every participant will earn them. The prosecution's account leaves out the speaker's direct qualification of the forecast.

citations.quote: each package that you purchase gets so many mining tokens that convert into OneCoin
We don't have any idea what's going to happen in the future. Nobody does.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The qualification applies to future coin value, not to the offer being promoted. The speaker still urges early entry because buying a package yields tokens for coins and earlier buyers purportedly receive more value. An uncertain price forecast does not neutralize that paid-mining pitch.

citations.quote: So the earlier you get into the 1Coin business, the better, because you're going to get more coins for value than later.
each package that you purchase gets so many mining tokens that convert into OneCoin

opening.argument: Judge, much of this presentation teaches the audience the speaker's model of cryptocurrency: how a finite supply is illustrated, how a wallet transfer would work, and how buyers might assign value to a digital asset. The speaker even identifies his arithmetic example as simplified. The invitation to a later seminar for more detail supports reading this as an introductory explanation of concepts and operations, rather than treating every described mechanism as a demand to purchase.

citations.quote: That's a very simplistic model of what cryptocurrency is.
All I need to know is his wallet email address. It's not an email address, it's a wallet address.
We do a trading seminar at the same time on Tuesday so please join us in learning more detail

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies real package and bonus descriptions, but describing how a proposed system operates is also what an introductory seminar does. The cited percentages explain the plan's rules; by themselves they do not establish that this is only a solicitation. The speaker expressly calls the presentation a high-level view and directs interested listeners to a more detailed session.

citations.quote: This is a very very high level view of the bonus plan. We break that down the more granular components on Tuesday evening.
it pays you a percentage of your team of those personally connected to you, four levels deep, four levels away from you

true_side_reply.rebuttal: An instructional format does not change the central offer. The explanation moves from concepts to priced packages whose tokens convert to coins, then promotes the larger package as a value proposition. It also presents compensation for sponsoring purchasers. Those are concrete purchase and recruitment appeals, not merely neutral operational examples.

citations.quote: each package that you purchase gets so many mining tokens that convert into OneCoin
this is a huge huge value proposition this tycoon package
He purchases one of the one coin packages that he pointed out from 100 euros to 5,000 euros plus a one-time 30 euro activation fee. I get a percentage for that.

opening.argument: Judge, the described transaction has identifiable prices and stated terms: packages supply mining tokens, and the speaker says holders can buy and sell coins on an exchange. Those details support an ordinary paid offering with a referral component. The presentation does not establish that a particular viewer deposits funds into a personal account, receives a guaranteed cash return, or loses the ability to sell. Risk and ambitious marketing are not, on their own, proof that the described product cannot function as offered.

citations.quote: pack at 130 Euro. Trader, 530. ProTrader, 1030. Executive, 3030. And Tycoon at 5,030.
each package that you purchase gets so many mining tokens that convert into OneCoin
all of us that hold owned OneCoin have the ability to buy and sell OneCoins within our exchange

rebuttal.rebuttal: Prices, token conversion, and team bonuses describe the offering, but the prosecution's citations do not show a guaranteed return or prove that coins cannot be sold. The speaker describes a buy-and-sell facility and acknowledges uncertainty about future value. A referral commission tied to a stated purchase does not, without more, establish that the underlying offering is fictitious.

citations.quote: all of us that hold owned OneCoin have the ability to buy and sell OneCoins within our exchange
We don't have any idea what's going to happen in the future. Nobody does.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A claim that holders can trade does not verify a functioning market or erase what viewers are urged to buy. The speaker says purchased packages produce mining tokens that become coins, while a larger package multiplies those tokens. The plan also pays an override on recruits' network bonuses. The absence of a guaranteed cash return does not remove these paid-mining and multilevel incentives.
